name: Ayodhya
text_clue: Capital of Kosala, a great country on the bank of the Sarayu
identification: Ayodhya, Uttar Pradesh: Ram Janmabhoomi site on the right bank of the Sarayu (Ghaghara)
paleo_note: Town on a stable Pleistocene upland; the Sarayu (Ghaghara) channel swings 4-7 km within its meander belt, so the river bank of Valmiki's time is uncertain by about ±5-7 km

name: Shringaverapura
text_clue: Guha's town on the Ganga where Rama crossed the river
identification: Shringverpur (Singraur), Prayagraj district: excavated site on the Ganga bank
paleo_note: No river shift documented: still on the Ganga's left bank; occupation TL-dated from c. 1035-875 BCE

name: Prayaga (Bharadvaja's ashram)
text_clue: Bharadvaja's hermitage at the joining (sandhi) of the Ganga and Yamuna, reached by evening
identification: Bharadwaj Ashram, Colonelganj, Prayagraj (proxy: Bharadwaj Park); confluence = Triveni Sangam
paleo_note: The confluence point moves seasonally and the Ganga moved west toward the fort in 1975-2000; the 'sandhi' is good to about ±1-2 km

name: Chitrakuta
text_clue: Hill 'ten krosha from here' (Prayaga) with the Mandakini river below it
identification: Kamadgiri hill, Chitrakoot (Kamta Nath temple); Mandakini at Ramghat

name: Atri and Anasuya's ashram
text_clue: Hermitage of Atri and Anasuya after leaving Chitrakuta
identification: Sati Anusuya ashram, Chitrakoot

name: Sharabhanga's ashram
text_clue: Hermitage in the Dandaka forest
identification: Sarbhanga Ashram village, Satna district (village-centre proxy)

name: Panchavati
text_clue: Two yojanas from Agastya's ashram, near the Godavari, by a madhuka forest and a hill
identification: Panchavati, Nashik (Sita Gufa / Kalaram temple) on the Godavari
paleo_note: Godavari incised in Deccan basalt at Nashik: channel stable at site scale

name: Agastya's ashram (north)
text_clue: Two yojanas from Panchavati
identification: Agasti temple, Akole, on the Pravara (tradition only)

name: Janasthana
text_clue: Khara's district around Panchavati
identification: Nashik region (no specific site; city centre as stand-in)

name: Pampa lake and Matanga's ashram
text_clue: Lake reached travelling west from Kabandha; Matanga's ashram on its west bank; Rishyamuka 'in front of' it
identification: Pampa Sarovar near Hampi / Anegundi
paleo_note: Tungabhadra in a granite-bedrock gorge: stable at site scale

name: Rishyamuka hill
text_clue: Sugriva's refuge hill near Pampa
identification: Rishyamukha hill across the Tungabhadra from Hampi

name: Kishkindha
text_clue: Vali and Sugriva's cave-city near Rishyamuka and Prasravana
identification: Anegundi on the Tungabhadra
paleo_note: Tungabhadra in a granite-bedrock gorge: stable at site scale

name: Prasravana hill on Malyavat
text_clue: Rama's monsoon camp on the back of Malyavat, not far from Kishkindha
identification: Malyavanta Raghunatha temple hill, Hampi

name: Malaya mountain (Agastya's peak)
text_clue: Agastya seated on the summit of Malaya, south of the Kaveri, before the Tamraparni
identification: Agastya Mala (Pothigai), 1,868 m, southern Western Ghats

name: Tamraparni river (mouth)
text_clue: Great river with crocodiles, island-studded, entering the sea; crossed after Malaya
identification: Thamirabarani river mouth at Punnakayal, Thoothukudi district
paleo_note: Delta prograded 7.5-8 km in ~2,000 yr. In the 1st millennium BCE the mouth was near Korkai, about 7.5 km west of today's (epoch coordinate 8.633°N, 78.067°E)

name: Golden gate (kavata) of the Pandyas
text_clue: Golden pearl-studded gate of the Pandyas, after the Tamraparni and before the sea
identification: Korkai, the early-historic Pandya pearl port near the Thamirabarani mouth (now inland)
paleo_note: Korkai was a coastal pearl port from the 3rd century BCE to the 5th century CE; now about 7.5 km inland

name: Mahendra mountain
text_clue: Set by Agastya at the sea, 'plunging into the ocean'; Hanuman's launch point; Rama climbs it and sees the sea
identification: Mahendragiri, Tirunelveli-Kanyakumari border: summit 1,654 m (GEBCO 1,555 m)

alternatives.name: Mahendragiri, Odisha (the Puranic Mahendra kula-parvata)
alternatives.note: fits Kishkindha 41's east-coast list, not the southern-sea episode

name: Southern ocean shore (army camp)
text_clue: The army reaches the shore forest (velavana) of the southern ocean after Mahendra
identification: Kanyakumari (Cape Comorin), the shore nearest Mahendragiri
paleo_note: Rocky cape: shoreline essentially fixed through the Holocene (GEBCO: <1 km change between -10 m and +1.5 m)

name: Setu: Indian end
text_clue: Causeway 100 yojanas long and 10 wide built by Nala 'in the middle of the ocean'
identification: Arichal Munai, tip of the Dhanushkodi spit: western end of Adam's Bridge (Rama Setu)
paleo_note: Spit and cays are mobile sand up to +3.5 m. During the +1.5-2 m highstand (6.5-5.5 ka) they were mostly awash, so the dry Indian end was the Rameswaram island core near 9.227°N, 79.340°E

name: Setu: Lanka end
text_clue: The causeway reaches the far shore
identification: Talaimannar, west tip of Mannar island: eastern end of Adam's Bridge
paleo_note: Mannar island is a low sand-and-reef island; its west tip migrates with the littoral drift

name: Lanka (the island)
text_clue: Island beyond Mahendra across the southern ocean, 'a full 100 yojanas' away, itself '100 yojanas long'
identification: Sri Lanka (geographic centre): the only island off the Tamraparni/Pandya coast joined to it by a shoal
paleo_note: Joined to India by land until sea level rose above the bridge sill (crest ~-3 m: c. 5200 BCE; rock ~-10 m: c. 6000 BCE)

name: Lanka city on Trikuta: candidate A
text_clue: City on the summit of Trikuta, seen from Suvela 'as if hanging in the sky'
identification: Central highlands: Sri Pada (Adam's Peak), fabled as Trikuta; 2,243 m

name: Lanka city on Trikuta: candidate B
text_clue: Name-based link Trikuta ~ Tiru-kona-malai
identification: Koneswaram on Swami Rock, Trincomalee (GEBCO ~30 m: not a mountain)

name: Lamba peak (Hanuman's landing)
text_clue: Hanuman lands on a peak of Mount Lamba, with ketaka, uddalaka and coconut trees
identification: Not identifiable: no Sri Lankan terrain of 100 m or more is in line of sight from the Setu landfall (GEBCO)

name: Suvela mountain
text_clue: Rama's first camp in Lanka; Lanka visible from its summit; a full-moon night
identification: Not identified by any source; the nearest hills of 300 m or more are ~148 km from the Setu landfall (GEBCO)

name: Ashoka Vatika tradition: Seetha Amman temple
text_clue: Sri Lankan Ramayana-trail tradition
identification: Ashoka Vatika tradition: Seetha Amman temple: Sita Eliya / Hakgala

name: Ravana Ella falls / cave tradition
text_clue: Sri Lankan Ramayana-trail tradition
identification: Ravana Ella falls / cave tradition: Ella

name: Vibhishana tradition: Kelaniya Raja Maha Vihara
text_clue: Sri Lankan Ramayana-trail tradition
identification: Vibhishana tradition: Kelaniya Raja Maha Vihara: near Colombo

name: Ritigala (Sanjivani tradition)
text_clue: Sri Lankan Ramayana-trail tradition
identification: Ritigala (Sanjivani tradition): 766 m isolated massif

name: Sigiriya (Ravana-palace folk tradition)
text_clue: Sri Lankan Ramayana-trail tradition
identification: Sigiriya (Ravana-palace folk tradition): 5th-century CE fortress

name: Ussangoda (Hanuman-fire tradition)
text_clue: Sri Lankan Ramayana-trail tradition
identification: Ussangoda (Hanuman-fire tradition): south coast

name: Rumassala (Sanjivani tradition)
text_clue: Sri Lankan Ramayana-trail tradition
identification: Rumassala (Sanjivani tradition): Galle

name: Wariyapola (Pushpaka airfield tradition)
text_clue: Sri Lankan Ramayana-trail tradition
identification: Wariyapola (Pushpaka airfield tradition): Kurunegala

name: Surya Siddhanta 'Lanka' (equator on Ujjain's meridian)
text_clue: Zero point of Indian astronomy: equator on the meridian of Ujjain
identification: Open ocean, 4,128 m deep (GEBCO): never land at any Quaternary sea level

name: Maldives hypothesis
text_clue: Proposed on long-yojana distance readings
identification: Male atoll: separated from India by a 2,592 m deep sill (GEBCO)

name: Central-India hypothesis (M. V. Kibe)
text_clue: Lanka at the Narmada source in the Amarkantak hills
identification: Amarkantak plateau: landlocked, ~700 km from the sea

name: Equator x Ujjain meridian at the Puranic end of Treta (~869 ka)
text_clue: Lanka placed where Ujjain's meridian meets the equator
identification: Today's location of that point after India-plate motion since 869 ka: open ocean, 4,308 m deep (GEBCO)
coord_source: Computed: NNR-MORVEL56 rotation of (0°, Ujjain's then-longitude)

name: Equatorial ridge candidate A: Huvadhu atoll plateau
valmiki_refs: Treta hypothesis (equatorial Lanka on the Chagos-Laccadive ridge)
text_clue: Largest land within 300 km of the equator at the Treta sea level (-90 m)
identification: Huvadhu atoll (Maldives) as an exposed limestone plateau: 3,737 km2, ~216 m above the Treta sea; 949 km from Mahendragiri (100 yojanas at 9.5 km); 2,286 m-deep sill to India

name: Equatorial ridge candidate B: Fuvahmulah plateau
text_clue: Second equatorial landmass at the Treta sea level
identification: Fuvahmulah (Maldives): 39 km2, ~109 m above the Treta sea; 1,065 km from Mahendragiri; channel to Huvadhu 1,995 m deep

name: Equatorial ridge candidate C: Addu atoll plateau
text_clue: Third equatorial landmass at the Treta sea level
identification: Addu atoll (Maldives): 206 km2, ~151 m above the Treta sea; 1,104 km from Mahendragiri; channel to Fuvahmulah 1,901 m deep

name: Drowned island: Great Chagos Bank
text_clue: Land at -90 m that is now reef and lagoon
identification: ~14,550 km2 limestone island at the Treta sea level (-90 m); reduced to reef ~10-8 ka by post-glacial sea-level rise; 5.6 km2 of islets today

name: Drowned island: Pitt Bank
text_clue: Land at -90 m that is now wholly submerged
identification: ~2,180 km2 at -90 m; drowned ~7.3 ka; no land today

name: Drowned island: Speakers Bank
text_clue: Land at -90 m that is now submerged
identification: ~980 km2 at -90 m; drowned ~8.1 ka; negligible land today

name: Near-circular abyssal basin (unexplained in GEBCO)
text_clue: Closed, near-circular basin with a slightly raised margin
identification: ~2,000 km2, 466 m deep below its rim at ~4,000 m depth; margin +32 m; needs a ship survey (GEBCO here is gravity-interpolated)

name: Near-circular abyssal basin (unexplained in GEBCO)
text_clue: Closed, near-circular basin with a slightly raised margin
identification: ~1,600 km2, 459 m deep below its rim at ~4,100 m depth; margin +75 m; needs a ship survey

name: Kumari Kandam test: Wadge Bank shelf south of Kanyakumari
valmiki_refs: (Tamil tradition of lands lost south of Kumari)
text_clue: Land said to have stretched south of Kanyakumari before the sea took it
identification: Real drowned land: ~8,600 km2 of shelf south of Kanyakumari was dry at the Treta sea level (-90 m), reaching only to ~7.4 N; beyond it the sea floor falls to 2,400 m at 6 N and 4,800 m at the equator (GEBCO)

name: Drowned plain of the Palk Bay
text_clue: Dry land joining India and Sri Lanka at low sea level
identification: ~26,000 km2 of plain between India and Sri Lanka, dry whenever the sea stood more than ~10 m below today

name: Mauritius (tested as Lanka)
text_clue: Island proposed by some as Lanka
identification: Volcanic island < 9 Myr old over the buried microcontinent 'Mauritia'; 20 S, 3,804 km from Mahendragiri (100 yojanas = 38 km each); the three-peaked Trois Mamelles is a coincidence of shape

name: Reunion (Mascarene hotspot island)
text_clue: Active hotspot volcano of the Mascarenes
identification: Summit 3,070 m; 4,039 km from Mahendragiri; barely larger at the Treta sea level

name: Drowned island: Saya de Malha Bank
text_clue: Bank that was a large island at low sea level
identification: ~18,500 km2 of land at the Treta sea level (-90 m), ~29,000 km2 at -128 m; no land today (NOAA ETOPO 2022)

name: Drowned island: Nazareth Bank
text_clue: Bank that was a large island at low sea level
identification: ~15,000 km2 of land at -90 m; no land today (NOAA ETOPO 2022)
